title: Rb1 and E2f4 derepress overlapping but non-identical cell-cycle programs in thalamic and selected GABAergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Rb1 induced a thalamic G1/S replication arm, including Dnmt1 logFC 1.5137015581130981 FDR 9.333656391552613e-10, Tipin 1.518267035484314 FDR 2.9339765482620998e-06, Prim1 2.7237536907196045 FDR 5.870073633290243e-05, and Lig1 1.9420918226242065 FDR 0.00016314637711243264 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with smaller Dnmt1-positive Rb1 responses in 155 MB Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba. E2f4 induced a parallel chromosome/repair arm in 151 TH marked by Aaas, Rad18, Tacc3, Tube1, Blm, Ddx11, and Polq.
biological_interpretation: Adult neurons preserve a measurable RB/E2F brake on cell-cycle genes, but Rb1 preferentially releases G1/S replication transcripts whereas E2f4 releases a partly distinct DREAM-like mitotic, chromosome, and repair module; E2f1 and E2f5 do not substitute for either active perturbation in the assayed neuronal states.
caveats: Rb1 mRNA itself was not FDR-depleted in the report, so downstream E2F-like induction is the engagement readout.
The assay measures RNA only; it does not prove DNA synthesis, pRB phosphorylation, apoptosis, or DREAM occupancy.

prior_expectation.summary: RB:E2F and DREAM/E2F4 repress related but separable cell-cycle waves; E2F4 participates in the p130-containing DREAM cell-cycle repressor complex; acute Rb inactivation in terminal neurons can trigger ectopic cell-cycle protein expression and neuronal loss
